result.title: What Makes a Latent Space Shared? Direct and Recoverable Compatibility in Motion VAEs
result.summary: A shared latent space is often assumed to make representations from different schemas directly interchangeable, yet sharing parameters, dimensionality, or a prior does not determine how corresponding instances are expressed in latent coordinates. We show that this assumption conflates recoverable correspondence, direct compatibility, and decoder reuse. In a controlled multi-schema motion VAE on HumanML3D, even identical inputs yield only $5.9$--$17.7\%$ raw Recall@1 and $0.221$--$0.484$ paired-token cosine, despite correspondence being almost perfectly recoverable after linear calibration. Cycle consistency strengthens recoverability but still leaves direct retrieval and token agreement near zero. In contrast, only $64$ paired clips raise raw Recall@1 to $88.4$--$90.3\%$ and token cosine to approximately $0.82$, making most post-hoc alignment unnecessary, although crossed decoding remains substantially worse than native reconstruction. We further find that reducing measured marginal discrepancy does not imply schema invariance. These results show that a shared backbone or prior does not ensure directly compatible latent coordinates, while limited paired correspondence can substantially improve direct compatibility in the tested setting.

AI.brief_summary: 在 HumanML3D 的多 schema 运动 VAE 中检验「共享 latent 空间」假设，发现共享骨干、维度或先验并不保证隐坐标可直接互换：原始 Recall@1 仅 5.9–17.7%，但线性校准后对应关系几乎可完全恢复。
AI.relevance_reason: 其对「可恢复对应」与「直接兼容」的区分，以及线性校准、循环一致性、少量配对片段微调等探针与干预手段，可能为 LVR 中判断 latent 状态是否被下游直接使用、跨模态隐表示对齐的评价提供可核查线索。
